Answer: C
Reason: The second chest X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates new, dense opacification in the right lower lung zone with obscuration of the right hemidiaphragm and mediastinal shift, consistent with progressive right lower lobe atelectasis/collapse. This progression from a relatively clearer initial film (Figure 4) to significant collapse is characteristic of a persistent endobronchial obstruction, such as foreign body aspiration, rather than transient mucous plugging or diffuse parenchymal disease.
